Bartermoot.name: Bartermoot
Bartermoot.text: Morning on the 14th (Garden Day). Representatives from the smaller towns and villages trade steel for lumber in ritual arrangement with the denizens of the Wood.

Boughmeal.name: Boughmeal
Boughmeal.text: Dawn until the afternoon on the 16th (Tithe Day). A market day held exclusively within the Wood, where artisans and merchants from all over the realm meet to trade their wares.

Dead Solstice.name: Dead Solstice
Dead Solstice.text: Midnight on the 10th (Tithe Day). Marks the shortest day of the year, and the midpoint of the Dead season.

Dry Equinox.name: Dry Equinox
Dry Equinox.text: Midnight on the 10th (Tithe Day). Marks the midpoint of the Dry season.

Dustset.name: Dustset
Dustset.text: Afternoon until midnight on the 9th (Song Day). A carnival marked by parades and masquerades, where participants wear masks to protect from dust and wind.

Ember.name: Ember
Ember.text: Evening on the 11th (Bathing Day). Pays homage to the setting sun and the hard work ahead preparing for the Dead season. Lantern release ceremonies are a common practice.

Firelight.name: Firelight
Firelight.text: All day on the 18th (Resting Day). A day of kite-flying, wind chimes, and noisemakers. At night, massive bonfires are lit as dancers perform impressive fire dances.

First Light.name: First Light
First Light.text: Dusk on the 24th (Resting Day). Commemorating the end of the first month of the new year. Torches and fire are lit all night, turning night to day.

First Plant.name: First Plant
First Plant.text: Afternoon of the 18th (Resting Day). A festival marking the beginning of planting season. Communities gather to plant the first seeds of the year together.

Float.name: Float
Float.text: All day on the 14th (Garden Day). Communities build and decorate enormous boats or rafts to float down rivers.

Gathering Night.name: Gathering Night
Gathering Night.text: Dusk on the 24th (Resting Day). Communities come together to collect and store the harvested crops, followed by a night of storytelling and music.

Gloam.name: Gloam
Gloam.text: Evening of the 24th (Resting Day). The final grand feast of the year, celebrating gratitude for the harvest, with the sun as centerpiece. Pregnancies are common.

Harvest Equinox.name: Harvest Equinox
Harvest Equinox.text: Midnight on the 10th (Tithe Day). Marks the midpoint of the Harvest season.

Harvest Festival.name: Harvest Festival
Harvest Festival.text: Afternoon on the 4th (Tithe Day). Celebrates the start of the harvest with feasting and communal gatherings to begin harvesting crops.

Highwater Fair.name: Highwater Fair
Highwater Fair.text: Dawn until midnight on the 1st (Market Day). A major trade event taking place when the waters are highest. Every major town and city celebrates with fairs and markets.

Lift the Veil.name: Lift the Veil
Lift the Veil.text: Midnight on the 9th (Song Day). The end of the Dead season is celebrated through solemn vows and humble gestures.

Parade of Ash.name: Parade of Ash
Parade of Ash.text: Afternoon on the 24th (Resting Day). In celebration of the final day of the Dry season, participants mark their faces with ash and play music. Most kinds of labor are frowned upon.

Splash Festival.name: Splash Festival
Splash Festival.text: 3 days starting on the 5th (Bathing Day to Market Day). Celebrates the abundance of water, with boat races, contests, gifts, and water blessings.

Storm Dance.name: Storm Dance
Storm Dance.text: Five days starting on the 19th (Market Day to Bathing Day). Dances and betrothals meant to please the masters of storm and rain for a fruitful Harvest season ahead.

The Golden Hind.name: The Golden Hind
The Golden Hind.text: Daylight hours of the 12th (Resting Day). Hunters from far and wide join a great hunt in search of a mythical stag amid great revelry.

Veil’s Edge.name: Veil’s Edge
Veil’s Edge.text: Afternoon to twilight on the 17th (Bathing Day). A day for honoring ancestors with offerings and prayers at family altars.

Waterwish.name: Waterwish
Waterwish.text: Lunchtime on the 14th (Garden Day). Participants write wishes on scrolls, place them into holes in a boulder, and roll it downhill. When it stops, any remaining wishes are thought to come true.

Wet Solstice.name: Wet Solstice
Wet Solstice.text: Midnight on the 10th (Tithe Day). Marks the longest day of the year, and the midpoint of the Wet season.

Whisper.name: Whisper
Whisper.text: Dawn to dusk on the 11th (Bathing Day). Speaking above a whisper is taboo. Silent auctions are common.
